long_biography.plain_text:
Businessman Ambrous Young grew up in Taiwan and served as a naval supply officer before studying engineering in England. On returning to Taipei, he established an aerospace consultancy, later moving to Hong Kong. His early commercial work included selling used aircraft parts around Asia, keeping travel costs down by sleeping in bus stations.

Young and his wife Annie also became founding members of the International SeaKeepers Society, providing resources for marine research, conservation and education. The organisation equipped vessels to gather information for ocean science. Its early programme used instruments to collect oceanic and atmospheric observations; later programmes arranged research expeditions with scientists.
